findings.problem: The simp interface for this homeomorphism is auto-generated and incomplete. The definition is a thin wrapper around `Topology.IsCoinducing.connectedComponentsHomeomorph`. The library already gives that lemma user-facing simp lemmas stated on classes, `connectedComponentsHomeomorph_mk` and `connectedComponentsHomeomorph_symm_mk_apply`. In contrast, `simps! apply` generates a lemma that unfolds the coercion, probably to `Continuous.connectedComponentsMap` applied to a continuity proof derived from the quotient-map argument. That exposes the implementation instead of the intended normal form `ConnectedComponents.mk (f x)`. The generated coercion lemma probably needs a further rewrite to reach that form. There is also no `symm` lemma, so `(f.connectedComponentsHomeomorph hf).symm (.mk (f x))` does not simplify to `.mk x`. The topological-level `_symm_mk_apply` lemma does not fire on the scheme-level wrapper without unfolding.
findings.proposed_change:
Drop `simps! apply` and state the canonical lemmas directly on the scheme-level definition, taking `X : Scheme` points `x : X`:
`@[simp] lemma Scheme.Hom.connectedComponentsHomeomorph_mk [GeometricallyConnected f] (hf : IsOpenMap f) (x : X) : f.connectedComponentsHomeomorph hf (.mk x) = .mk (f x) := rfl`
and
`@[simp] lemma Scheme.Hom.connectedComponentsHomeomorph_symm_mk_apply ... : (f.connectedComponentsHomeomorph hf).symm (.mk (f x)) = .mk x`.
The second one can be proved by `Topology.IsCoinducing.connectedComponentsHomeomorph_symm_mk_apply`, or by injectivity as in that lemma. Alternatively, keep `simps` but add `@[simps! symm_apply]`. The cleaner option is to mirror the two lemmas already in `Mathlib/Topology/Homeomorph/Lemmas.lean`.
findings.benefit: Terms of the form `f.connectedComponentsHomeomorph hf (.mk x)` and its inverse would simplify to `.mk (f x)` and `.mk x`, matching the topological-level normal form. The simp set would not leak the proof-term internals of `Continuous.connectedComponentsMap`.
